questions.stem_html:
A 47-year-old man has recurrent sinus pain, bloody nasal discharge, cough with hemoptysis, and hematuria. CT shows cavitary pulmonary nodules. Creatinine is elevated, and urinalysis reveals red-cell casts. Proteinase-3 ANCA is strongly positive. Kidney immunofluorescence shows little or no immune deposition.

Which histologic finding is most characteristic outside the kidney?

options.text_html: Eosinophil-rich granulomas in a patient with severe asthma
Necrotizing granulomatous inflammation involving small- and medium-sized vessels
Immune-complex deposition with fibrinoid necrosis and low serum complement
Segmental transmural inflammation limited to medium arteries without granulomas

questions.explanation_html: GPA causes necrotizing granulomatous inflammation in the upper and lower respiratory tracts and pauci-immune necrotizing glomerulonephritis. PR3-ANCA is a common associated marker. The upper-airway, pulmonary, and renal pattern with PR3-ANCA and pauci-immune kidney injury is classic for necrotizing granulomatous vasculitis.

wrong_choice_explanations.1: Noncaseating granulomas suggest sarcoidosis and do not explain pauci-immune glomerulonephritis.
wrong_choice_explanations.2: That pattern is characteristic of eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: GPA is typically pauci-immune and complement levels are often normal.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: This more closely resembles polyarteritis nodosa, which usually spares glomeruli.

questions.educational_objective: Distinguish GPA from other vasculitides by its upper-airway disease, cavitary lung nodules, pauci-immune glomerulonephritis, PR3-ANCA, and necrotizing granulomas.
